$description: The RFC 8628 device flow's waiting room: the code GitHub minted, the page to type it into, and a Cancel. A `jx-dialog`, so the platform owns modality, Escape, focus restoration and the backdrop — and it is the reason the dialog has no confirm button at all: the answer arrives from GitHub over a poll rather than from anything the reader can press here, so a primary button would be a control with nothing to do. Nothing in this document talks to GitHub: `github/github-auth.ts` keeps the client id, the poll loop, its failure budget and every report the three outcomes raise.

style.$description: Four `.github-auth-*` rules in `styles/overlays.css` become the parts below, and two things in them do not travel. `.github-auth-dialog`'s `padding: 16px 0` was the card's own body padding drawn by hand, and `jx-dialog` already pads its body; `.github-auth-dialog p { font-size: 13px }` was a body size this surface picked for itself, and what the paragraphs now inherit is the dialog's own `--jx-text-md`. The `8px 0` margins go with them — the column is a flex column with a gap, so a margin between two rows would be a second opinion about the same space. The code keeps its 24px, which is above the token scale on purpose: it is a string the reader has to copy onto another screen, and reading it out loud is the whole job of this dialog.

& [part=\"code\"].$description: `<code>`, not a styled `<div>`: this is a literal string to be transcribed, and the element that says so is also the one a reader's own stylesheet and a screen reader's character-by-character mode already know about.

& [part=\"link\"].$description: The blue this carried as a `var(--accent, …)` fallback is gone: `--accent` is declared on `:root` in `styles/tokens.css`, so the fallback could only ever have painted when the token was missing — which is a theme fault to fix rather than a colour to hard-code.
